CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the management of generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, persistent fatigue, and tension-type headaches, along with a review of recent symptom fluctuations.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his scheduled follow-up appointment, reporting a mixed response regarding his symptoms over the past month. He acknowledges a slight increase in the frequency of his tension-type headaches, now occurring approximately twice a week, with an intensity rating fluctuating between 3 to 4 out of 10. He attributes this change to heightened work-related stress and has noted that the pain is responsive to his current regimen of ibuprofen.
Sleep quality has seen a slight decline, with Mr. Smith averaging closer to 6 hours of sleep per night. He reports that while he still finds gabapentin helpful, he has experienced more frequent nocturnal awakenings and difficulty returning to sleep. The mindfulness meditation and deep-breathing exercises remain part of his routine, but he expresses concern that they may not be sufficient given the recent stressors.
Persistent fatigue continues to be an issue, particularly in the mornings. Mr. Smith notes that while he maintains his exercise routine, he feels less motivated and more fatigued post-exercise than previously. He denies any new symptoms such as chest pain, shortness of breath, or significant changes in appetite.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 250 mg daily (continued) 2. Trazodone 50 mg at bedtime (continued) 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime (continued) 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued) 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (continued) 6. Amitriptyline 50 mg nightly (continued) 7. Topiramate 100 mg daily (continued) 8. Lorazepam 1 mg as needed (continued) 9. Gabapentin 100 mg at bedtime (continued)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, where he is currently facing increased project demands contributing to his elevated stress levels. He remains committed to his physical fitness regime, participating in running and yoga, which he believes are crucial for his overall well-being. His dietary habits remain consistent, with an emphasis on balanced nutrition, and he continues to abstain from alcohol while limiting caffeine intake.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Increased anxiety levels noted; sleep disruptions reported; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms. - Neurological: Increased headache frequency; no dizziness or visual disturbances reported. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue noted, particularly in the mornings, with no fever or weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 118/75 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.4F - General: Alert, oriented, appears well-groomed; mood appears anxious but cooperative. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed; headache tenderness noted in the temporal region. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears anxious with moderate distress.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 250 mg daily. Consider increasing the dosage if anxiety levels do not stabilize. Lorazepam usage remains as needed for acute episodes. 2. Insomnia: Reassess the efficacy of trazodone and melatonin; consider adjusting gabapentin dosage if sleep disruptions persist. Monitor for any adverse effects or further sleep disturbances. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Increase ibuprofen dosage as needed for headache relief. Consider adding a preventive strategy if frequency continues to increase. Continue topiramate at 100 mg daily and amitriptyline at 50 mg nightly. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage Mr. Smith to maintain a sleep diary to identify patterns. Explore the possibility of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for insomnia and anxiety management. If fatigue persists or worsens, further evaluation for underlying causes will be necessary.
Follow-up appointment is scheduled for 2029-09-01 to monitor symptom changes, evaluate treatment adjustments, and address any new concerns. Mr. Smith is advised to implement additional stress management strategies and to maintain a headache diary to track triggers and treatment response.
